Description: The Equine Practice Company (TEPC) is an Australian veterinary education business operating globally. We generate revenue across multiple platforms — Kajabi (3 accounts), WooCommerce (2 websites), Stripe (5 accounts), and PayPal. We need a data engineer to build an automated monthly financial consolidation and reporting system from scratch. About the project: Every month our bookkeeper manually pulls 10 exports from three platforms, consolidates and matches them row by row, calculates revenue accruals and accounts receivable, and produces a set of reporting worksheets and workpapers. This takes several hours per month and depends on fragile manual processes. We need this automated end to end. Data comes in, rules are applied, outputs are produced, exceptions go to a human for review. The bookkeeper's job becomes reviewing and approving rather than building. What we will provide Revenue Recognition Rulebook (13 sections covering all program types, edge cases, and exception handling) 7 CFO training video transcripts explaining the full workpaper logic in detail Sample data files from two closed months (real data, figures available under NDA) A bookkeeper (CA, BAS Agent) available for validation throughout the build A CFO available for financial logic questions Full SOP documentation What we need built Phase 1 — Data foundation and automation (weeks 1-4) Ingest all 10 monthly source files: 3 Kajabi CSVs, 2 WooCommerce XLSXs, 5 Stripe CSVs, plus PayPal Build a central data layer (PostgreSQL or equivalent) — raw data preserved, stable source IDs, every transformation traceable back to its source record Build order-to-payment matching logic (WooCommerce matched by order ID; Kajabi matched by email + date with timezone offset handling) Handle multi-currency conversion (6 currencies, AUD reporting) using Stripe converted amounts Classify all transactions against a program lookup table (113 program configurations) Calculate revenue accrual per program per month across all recognition types: subscriptions monthly and annual, fixed-term payment plans, one-time purchases with defined access periods and products Calculate accounts receivable per client per program Calculate active client count and new client count (NCC) per program per month Handle refunds, re-enrolments, payment plan instalments, and cancelled/failed order exclusions Allocate transactions across two legal entities Generate Xero-ready journal entry output Phase 2 — Validation (weeks 5-6) Back-test all rules against closed months (July 2024 to May 2026) Compare output line by line against what our bookkeeper and CFO actually produced historically Document and explain every variance — not absorb it CFO sign-off before proceeding to Phase 3 Phase 3 — Interface, documentation, and handover (weeks 7-8) Simple drag-and-drop file upload interface usable by a non-technical bookkeeper (or similar process) Hosted solution — suggest your preferred approach Full technical documentation and annotated code Step-by-step user guide for the bookkeeper Handover session with bookkeeper and CFO Support through the first live month-end close The complexity you need to understand before quoting This is not a standard ecommerce reconciliation. Specific challenges: No shared key between Kajabi and Stripe — Kajabi's Invoice ID is empty in every export and its Receipt ID does not match any Stripe charge. Matching falls back to email and date, which drifts due to timezone differences (Kajabi records local time, Stripe records UTC) and customers using different email addresses across platforms Three source schemas with inconsistent column structures — the same column holds different data depending on the platform the row came from, and column order varies between accounts within the same platform Revenue recognition across 113 program configurations with different rules per type Multi-currency with country price parity — the same program is priced differently by region Two legal entities requiring separate allocation Monthly reporting currently depends on the prior month's file via VLOOKUP chains — this fragility must be eliminated by storing and recomputing from raw source data PayPal transactions have no Stripe record and require approximation logic for FX and fees Approximately 18% of transactions carry edge cases requiring exception handling and human review If any of the above is unfamiliar, this project is not the right fit. Who will succeed: Has built financial data pipelines or accounting integrations before — not just general web development Understands accrual accounting at a working level — you do not need to be an accountant, but you must know what deferred revenue, accounts receivable, and revenue recognition mean in practice Has worked with Xero API or Xero journal entry imports Has experience with Stripe data structures and the Stripe CSV export format Communicates precisely in English — financial logic cannot be discussed vaguely Provides regular progress updates — daily or every other day during the build Can work independently alongside a bookkeeper and CFO without needing the CEO involved in day-to-day decisions Has references from similar financial automation or accounting integration work What we do not want: Proposals that treat this as a simple CSV processing job Vague scoping — "I will build a dashboard" without specifying what is in it will not be reviewed Developers who disappear for a week and reappear with something that does not match the brief Anyone who cannot explain the difference between a new enrolment, a re-enrolment, and a payment plan instalment — this distinction drives client counting and revenue recognition throughout the system Budget: USD $3,000-$6,000 for the full project across all three phases, paid in milestones tied to deliverables. Milestone structure is negotiable but must track delivery — we do not pay large amounts upfront. We are open to an ongoing monthly retainer for maintenance and rule updates after delivery How to apply: Your proposal must address all four of the following or it will not be reviewed: 1) One specific example of a financial data pipeline or accounting integration you have built. Describe what it did, what the data sources were, what the output was, and what the hardest part was. 2) Your answer to this technical question: our monthly reporting currently uses VLOOKUP formulas that reference the prior month's saved workbook to restore baselines after rows shift. How would your data architecture handle a rule correction in month 6 that needs to flow back through months 1 to 5 without manual restatement of historical figures? 3) Your proposed timeline broken into the three phases above, with specific milestones and what gets delivered at each one. 4)Your rate, milestone payment structure, and total cost in USD. Proposals that do not address all four points will not be opened. Full Revenue Recognition Rulebook and CFO training transcripts provided under NDA to shortlisted candidates only. You will join a company that is excellence-driven with a supportive culture that already has a team in the Philippines

Description: Lead Nutritionist Foodini | Full-time | Remote (US) | Reports to the COO About Foodini Foodini is a dietary intelligence platform. We give restaurants, hotels, stadiums, and food-service operators ingredient-level control over their menu data so guests with allergies and dietary needs know exactly what is safe to eat, and so operators can meet a fast-moving set of allergen and nutrition disclosure laws. Our engine, DietaryAI, pulls menu, recipe, and ingredient data straight out of the inventory and recipe systems operators already run, including CrunchTime, Restaurant365, MarginEdge, Craftable, Meez, and COGS-Well. Every menu is then verified by a registered dietitian before it reaches a guest. That combination, AI at the ingredient level with dietitians in the loop, is the solution the restaurant industry needs to meet the new wave of regulation, along with the preferences of today's consumer. We work with Hungry Howie's, Compass Group, Marriott, José Andrés Group, Bartaco, J. Alexander's, Bluestone Lane, Saxbys, Sweetfin, and Areas USA, and we launched the first allergen-filtered concession ordering at a Major League Baseball stadium. Fast Company named us #9 in its 2026 Most Innovative Companies list for Restaurants, Dining & Food Services. We are headquartered in Los Angeles with a global team. The role We are hiring a Lead Nutritionist to oversee nutrition calculation at Foodini, guide our team of dietitians, and set the standards behind what operators can say about their menus. Our depth today is in allergens. Nutrition is the next layer, and we are not building it the traditional way. The traditional way is one recipe at a time. A dietitian hand-keys ingredients into a database, resolves each one against a reference entry, applies yield and retention factors from a table, and produces a static number. It takes weeks per menu, it costs real money, and it is stale the moment a supplier changes a formulation or a chef swaps an ingredient. Most operators end up with a PDF that was accurate eighteen months ago. We are building the other version. Nutrition calculated from the recipe and inventory data already flowing out of an operator's back-of-house systems, matched and modeled by DietaryAI at the ingredient level, verified by our dietitians, and recalculated when the underlying data changes rather than once a year. The AI does the matching, the modeling, and the scale. Your team does the judgment, the standards, and the verification that makes the output defensible. The part nobody has built yet Nutrition data has always been treated as an obligation, something a restaurant publishes because a regulator says it must. It is also demand data, and that is the half of this job we are most excited about. Guests are ordering for protein. Guests on GLP-1 medications want smaller portions, more protein, and more fiber, and they are a fast-growing share of every dining room in the country. Operators are already selling items that fit what those guests want, and they have no way to identify them, let alone market them. The nutrition data sits in a compliance PDF while the menu says nothing. Once nutrition is calculated at the ingredient level across an entire menu, that changes. You define what qualifies: the threshold that makes an item high protein, the standard Foodini will stand behind for GLP-1 friendly, where FDA nutrient content claim rules govern the language and where we are setting the definition ourselves because no one has. Those standards then drive how operators merchandise their menus. No one in this industry has done this. Getting it right is a nutrition problem and a commercial one at the same time, and you would own both halves. What you will do -Own Foodini's nutritional analysis methodology: reference database selection, ingredient matching standards, yield and retention factors, and cooking method adjustments -Set direction for our dietitian team and act as the technical authority they check their work against -Define the nutrition-based attributes Foodini stands behind, including high protein and GLP-1 friendly, and the thresholds, evidence, and claim language behind each one -Work side by side with engineering to encode that methodology into DietaryAI, and to decide where automated calculation is trustworthy and where it must escalate to a human -Set the confidence thresholds and QA process that catch errors before a client or a guest ever sees them, and own accuracy as a measurable standard -Define how nutrition data stays current as recipes, suppliers, and inventory records change -Make sure our outputs meet FDA menu labeling requirements, nutrient content claim rules, and state allergen disclosure laws, including California SB-68 -Work with client-facing teams during onboarding, when a brand's recipe data is messy and someone has to make the right call -Serve as Foodini's nutrition voice with clients, partners, and in industry conversations What you bring -Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) credential, or an equivalent degree in nutrition or food science with directly comparable analysis experience -Real experience calculating nutrition for restaurant or food-service menus, not just clinical or consumer work. You have handled recipes with vague specs, regional variation, and suppliers who change formulations without telling anyone -Working knowledge of FDA menu labeling requirements and nutrient analysis software such as Genesis R&D, Nutritionix, or ESHA. You know what those tools do well and where they run out of road -A read on where consumer nutrition is actually heading, from GLP-1 medications to protein and fiber demand, and the judgment to tell a durable shift from a fad -Genuine interest in what AI can and cannot do here. You do not need to have built a model, but you should want to spend your time teaching a system your judgment instead of repeating it by hand -Comfort with data at scale: spreadsheets with tens of thousands of rows, structured data, and the instinct to ask where a number came from -Judgment about accuracy. You know where published data is reliable, where it is not, and how to document the difference -Readiness to guide other dietitians and set standards they work to. Formal management experience is welcome but not required Nice to have -Experience with back-of-house systems like CrunchTime, Restaurant365, MarginEdge, Craftable, or Meez -SQL, Python, or a similar tool you use to check your own work -Experience building nutrition data for enterprise or multi-unit brands -Menu development, culinary R&D, or marketing experience alongside the analysis work -Familiarity with allergen compliance alongside nutrition Why this role Menu nutrition information today is mostly a PDF nobody can use, produced by a process that has not meaningfully changed in twenty years. The people who need it most, guests managing allergies, celiac disease, diabetes, or specific nutritional targets, are the ones least served by it. This is a chance to rebuild that process rather than run it, and then to do something with the output the industry has never done. The methodology you set becomes the platform's methodology across every operator we serve. The standards you write for what counts as high protein or GLP-1 friendly become how thousands of menu items get presented to guests. Very few nutrition roles anywhere let you set a definition and see it reach that many tables.
